source.note: Six photorealistic clips, supplied as a zip and generated outside this pipeline from the prompts recorded on each segment. They are independent shots (no shared first/last frames), so segments are joined with dissolves.

caption.title: Foundations
caption.line: January 1887 · Four masonry piers on the Champ de Mars

segments.prompt: Photorealistic cinematic footage, natural daylight. Fixed low camera on a tripod, no camera movement. Construction of four limestone foundation piers: large cut limestone blocks are lowered gently from just above, one after another, and settle softly into each of the four excavated pits, stacking into four solid low masonry piers. The wooden survey stakes and strings sink smoothly into the gravel and disappear. Every block eases into place and settles; nothing pops or appears suddenly. Clouds drift very slowly. Calm, precise, steady motion. No people, no cranes, no vehicles, no text.

camera.move: close under the arches, then a wide pull-back

segments.rangeNote: Frames 51-137 are skipped: the clip builds well past the first platform there and then shrinks back to it. The wide shot is short, so its last frame is held under the dissolve into the next segment.
segments.prompt: Photorealistic cinematic footage, natural daylight. One continuous, steady dolly-out: the camera travels straight backward and slightly upward for the entire shot, moving far away from the construction site, so the site becomes smaller and smaller and settles low in the centre of the frame under a large open sky. The camera never moves forward and never tilts up. While the camera pulls back, only the base of the Eiffel Tower is built: four riveted wrought-iron lattice legs, painted bronze-brown, rise from the four limestone piers, girders gliding in from slightly offset positions and settling into place, the legs leaning inward until the arches close and the square first platform with its railing locks together on top. Construction stops at the first platform: nothing at all is built above it, and its top stays flat, open and empty with only sky above. The shot ends as a wide view of the finished base, small in the frame. Every piece eases in and settles; nothing pops or appears suddenly. No people, no cranes, no vehicles, no text.

Photorealistic cinematic footage, natural daylight. Very slow, steady dolly-in from a low angle; the squat iron structure grows slightly larger in the frame. A single short second tier is added on top of the flat platform: four short inclined riveted iron lattice columns glide in from slightly offset positions and settle into place, rising only a little way, braced with cross-beams, and then one small square deck with a railing slides together on top of them and locks in. That is all that happens. The structure stays low, wide and squat with a flat top, and the sky above it stays empty. The arched base stays solid and unchanged. Every piece eases in and settles; nothing pops or appears suddenly. No people, no cranes, no vehicles, no text.

segments.rangeNote: Frames 151-215 are dropped: the clip finishes the cabin and spire there, which the next segment builds.
segments.prompt: Photorealistic cinematic drone footage. One continuous, smooth crane and orbit shot: the camera rises steadily from the low angle near the ground, orbiting around the tower as it climbs, and ends high in the air in an aerial view looking down at the tower corner-on, with the Champ de Mars lawns and Haussmann buildings spread out below. During the move, the tall tapering upper shaft of the Eiffel Tower assembles above the second platform: riveted iron lattice segments glide in from slightly offset positions and settle into place one above another, the shaft growing taller and narrower. Every piece eases in and settles; nothing pops or appears suddenly. The light warms gradually from clear daylight to golden hour, the sun low on the left, long soft shadows stretching across the lawns, clouds turning peach. No people, no cranes, no vehicles, no text.

Photorealistic cinematic aerial footage. Fixed aerial camera, perfectly steady, no camera movement. The Eiffel Tower is almost finished: its four legs, both platforms and the whole tall lattice shaft are already built and stay completely solid and unchanged for the entire shot. Nothing is removed, nothing shrinks, nothing is rebuilt. Only three small pieces are added at the very tip of the tower, one after another: first the small top cabin is lowered from just above and settles onto the open top of the shaft, then the slender spire settles onto the cabin, then the thin antenna settles onto the spire. Each piece eases in and settles; nothing pops or appears suddenly. Meanwhile the sun sinks slowly below the horizon on the left and the sky shifts smoothly from golden hour to dusk: peach and rose at the horizon, lavender and slate blue above. The clouds drift away and thin out. The light on the lawns and buildings cools and dims gently. No lights switch on. No people, no cranes, no vehicles, no text.

Photorealistic cinematic aerial footage. Fixed aerial camera, perfectly steady, no camera movement. Night falls over Paris and the Eiffel Tower lights up. The dusk sky deepens smoothly to deep indigo, with a faint violet glow at the horizon, and a few stars fade in. Warm golden floodlights switch on progressively along the tower from the base upward: first the four legs and arches glow, then the first platform, the second platform, the tall shaft, and finally a bright beacon ignites at the antenna tip. A soft golden glow spreads across the plaza beneath the tower. Warm lights come on in the windows of the Haussmann buildings and along the paths. The geometry of the tower and city stays perfectly unchanged; only the light changes, smoothly and gradually. No people, no vehicles, no text.
